articles.title: Antonio Brown makes provocative Erika Kirk remark exactly one year after Charlie Kirk’s assassination
articles.summary: NFL News: Antonio Brown has sparked a fresh wave of controversy with a provocative post about Erika Kirk, shared on the first anniversary of her husband Charlie.
articles.body: Antonio Brown has sparked a fresh wave of controversy with a provocative post about Erika Kirk, shared on the first anniversary of her husband Charlie Kirk’s assassination. The former NFL star questioned her private life in a post that quickly drew attention online. Coming exactly one year after Charlie’s death, the timing has added another layer of controversy to Brown’s already long history of polarizing social media activity.Antonio Brown sparks backlash with controversial Erika Kirk post on Charlie Kirk anniversaryAntonio Brown has once again drawn attention for a social media post, this time involving Erika Kirk on a deeply sensitive date. On September 10, the first anniversary of Charlie Kirk’s assassination, a post attributed to Brown asked a blunt and highly personal question about the widow’s private life.The post read:“Do u guys think Erika Kirk has had s*x in the past year”The timing immediately made the post more controversial. September 10 marked one year since Charlie Kirk was fatally shot while speaking at Utah Valley University in Utah. His widow, Erika, has spent the past year grieving his death while also stepping into a much more prominent leadership role at Turning Point USA.The question posted about Erika was not accompanied by evidence or any claim based on reporting. It was simply speculation about her private life. That distinction matters, particularly because Erika has openly described the emotional weight of losing her husband.In a recent reflection, she wrote about learning to live with grief and described it as something that can feel lonely. She also said she continues to trust her faith while raising the couple's children and carrying Charlie's legacy.The screenshot also shows other users pushing back on Brown's post. One response called attention to the fact that Erika is a widow and argued that the question crossed a line. Another user responded with a Bible passage from Luke.The reactions underline why the post attracted attention beyond Brown's own followers. It appeared on a day when public discussion around Erika was largely centered on remembrance, grief and Charlie Kirk's legacy.Antonio Brown's controversial history keeps him in the spotlightThe latest post also fits a broader pattern that has followed Brown since the end of his NFL career. Once one of the league's most productive wide receivers, Brown has become increasingly known for controversial statements, legal problems and unpredictable social media activity.Brown's football career ended in 2021 after his dramatic exit from a Tampa Bay Buccaneers game. He later faced a series of legal and financial problems, including a Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in 2024. In 2025, authorities charged him with second-degree attempted murder over a shooting incident outside a Miami boxing event. Brown pleaded not guilty, and the case remained active in 2026.That history has changed the way many people view his online comments. A post that might otherwise disappear into the fast-moving social media cycle can quickly become a headline when it comes from someone with Brown's reputation.His latest remarks about Erika Kirk are therefore less about establishing anything about her personal life and more about another controversial moment involving the former NFL star. There is no verified information in the post establishing that Erika has or has not had a sexual relationship since Charlie's death.For Erika, meanwhile, the anniversary carried a very different meaning. She marked the year since Charlie's death while continuing to navigate grief, motherhood and the responsibility of leading the organization he founded.Brown's post may generate plenty of online reaction, but speculation about a grieving widow's private life should not be mistaken for news.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why is Josh Jacobs’ Packers future suddenly uncertain? The RB’s legal trouble puts Matt LaFleur in a difficult spot
articles.summary: NFL News: Josh Jacobs’ future with the Green Bay Packers has taken another turn. The running back pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges in Wisconsin on Thur.
articles.body: Josh Jacobs’ future with the Green Bay Packers has taken another turn. The running back pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges in Wisconsin on Thursday, September 10, but Matt LaFleur says his view of Jacobs has not changed.The Packers coach also made it clear that the team will wait for the NFL to finish its investigation before making any decision about Jacobs. For now, the 28-year-old remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and cannot play or practice. Why is Matt LaFleur standing by Josh Jacobs despite the legal case?LaFleur addressed Jacobs’ situation ahead of the Packers’ season opener against the Minnesota Vikings. When reporters asked whether his opinion of Jacobs had changed, the Packers coach gave a blunt answer.“No,” LaFleur said while speaking to reporters. He then pointed to his relationship with Jacobs and his view of the running back’s character.“I know the guy, and I know the character of the guy. … Unfortunately, situations occur in life, and it’s just an unfortunate situation.”LaFleur did not stop there. When reporters asked why Green Bay would keep Jacobs on the roster if he is found guilty, he refused to speculate.“I’m not gonna get into any of this until the league completes their investigation,” LaFleur said during the same media session.That leaves the Packers in a holding pattern. Green Bay has not released Jacobs, while general manager Brian Gutekunst also said the team hopes he can play this season.“I think that’s to be seen,” Gutekunst said while discussing Jacobs’ 2026 status. “Certainly hopeful that he will, and certainly would expect that, but we’re gonna let that process play out.”Could Josh Jacobs still miss games despite his no-contest plea?Jacobs pleaded no contest on September 10 to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges. The agreement gave him a $1,000 fine and court-ordered conditions for the battery charges. The criminal-damage charge received a 12-month deferred disposition and could get dismissed if Jacobs meets the conditions.Those conditions include avoiding contact with the victim, attending counseling, paying restitution and staying out of trouble. Jacobs also remains under criminal-justice supervision.“I fully understand the seriousness of the situation and I take full responsibility,” Jacobs said, per ESPN, following the plea.However, the end of the criminal case does not end the NFL’s review. The league placed Jacobs on the Commissioner’s Exempt List in August while it investigates under its personal-conduct policy.The NFL confirmed on September 10 that there had been no change to Jacobs’ status. He cannot practice or play, although he can receive his salary and use team facilities with Green Bay’s permission.Jacobs was arrested on May 26 after police investigated a disturbance involving him and his girlfriend at his Wisconsin home. Prosecutors later filed only the two misdemeanor charges.Now, the NFL has the next call. A suspension remains possible, but the league has not announced one. Therefore, despite LaFleur’s public support, Josh Jacobs’ 2026 season still depends on the outcome of the NFL investigation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers knew Brittani was "the one" in 2017. Then spent years dating the wrong people: "My biggest regret"
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Rodgers says he now understands that the relationship he wanted most was in front of him years before his best-known romances began. Rodgers fir.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers says he now understands that the relationship he wanted most was in front of him years before his best-known romances began. Rodgers first met his now-wife Brittani in 2017, but she was preparing to return to Europe. Looking back, the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback says his biggest regret was not asking her to stay or proposing at the time. Instead, he threw himself into football and later entered high-profile relationships with Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley. Rodgers now says he knew Brittani was the person who could change his life, even when distance kept them apart.Why does Aaron Rodgers regret not proposing to Brittani in 2017?Aaron Rodgers was unusually direct about the missed opportunity during his appearance on Cam Heyward’s Not Just Football podcast."At the time, she was leaving the States and going back to Europe," Rodgers said. "And my biggest regret is not begging her to stay or proposing right there."Her departure affected him more than he expected. Rodgers said the decision sent him into what he described as a "tailspin" and left him "emotionally unavailable" for the next seven or eight years."I'd met the person that was going to change my life," he explained. "After that, I just poured everything into football."The comment adds an important layer to Rodgers' dating history. He was not simply looking back at an old relationship with regret. He said he already believed Brittani was the right person at the time, yet still allowed the relationship to slip away.What happened between Aaron Rodgers and Danica Patrick?About a year after meeting Brittani, Rodgers began dating Danica Patrick. Their relationship became public in 2018 and lasted until 2020.Rodgers has now offered a blunt account of that period, saying the relationship eventually lacked intimacy and that the pair tried couples therapy before splitting.His latest comments suggest he was entering that relationship after already carrying unresolved feelings from Brittani's departure. Rodgers did not say Patrick was simply a replacement, but his timeline makes clear that Brittani remained significant in his mind.Why did Aaron Rodgers and Shailene Woodley break up?Rodgers later became engaged to Shailene Woodley. Their relationship was publicly confirmed in 2021, but the engagement eventually ended.Rodgers has disputed Woodley's version of their breakup and recently gave his own account of what went wrong. He said the relationship had deteriorated much earlier than the eventual split suggested.That relationship now sits in striking contrast with how Rodgers describes Brittani. With Woodley, the engagement became public and ended under intense scrutiny. With Brittani, Rodgers ultimately chose privacy.When did Aaron Rodgers and Brittani get married?Rodgers confirmed in 2025 that he had secretly married Brittani, revealing little about the ceremony or their private life. He has since spoken warmly about the relationship, calling her an "incredible" wife and saying unconditional love changed his outlook on other parts of his life.He also credited Brittani with helping him reconnect with his family after years of estrangement. Rodgers said her influence was not about pressure, but about giving him a different perspective on his relationships."She was engaged, then I got engaged, and luckily, for me, we came back together," Rodgers said.For Rodgers, that reunion appears to have changed the meaning of everything that came before it. The relationships with Patrick and Woodley were highly public, but the relationship he now describes as life-changing began quietly in 2017. The quarterback's regret is not that he dated other people. It is that he says he already knew who mattered most and still let her leave.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chicago Bears quietly make a $33.75 million move that keeps one of their most important stars in Chicago
articles.summary: NFL News: The Chicago Bears have made a significant commitment to D’Andre Swift, agreeing to a three-year, $33.75 million contract extension that keeps the runn.
articles.body: The Chicago Bears have made a significant commitment to D’Andre Swift, agreeing to a three-year, $33.75 million contract extension that keeps the running back under contract through the 2029 season. The deal includes $27.5 million guaranteed and comes just before Chicago opens its 2026 season against the Carolina Panthers. Swift was entering the final year of his previous contract, making his future one of the team’s bigger financial decisions heading into the season. Instead of waiting, the Bears chose to settle the issue now. That decision also gives head coach Ben Johnson another key piece to build around in the coming years.Why did the Bears give D’Andre Swift a $33.75 million extension?The timing says plenty about how Chicago views Swift. The 27-year-old is coming off the most productive rushing season of his career, with 1,087 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns in 2025. He also added 34 catches for 299 yards and another touchdown. His 1,386 yards from scrimmage marked another career high.That production gave the Bears a strong reason to act before Swift entered a contract year. He originally joined Chicago on a three-year, $24 million deal in 2024 after spending time with the Detroit Lions and Philadelphia Eagles. His first season in Chicago produced 1,345 yards from scrimmage and six touchdowns, followed by an even better 2025 campaign.The new deal raises Swift’s average annual salary by more than $3 million compared with his previous contract, according to NFL.com. More importantly for Chicago, it removes the uncertainty surrounding its starting running back for several seasons.What does Swift’s new contract mean for the Bears?The move is about more than rewarding one strong season. Chicago is trying to build a stable offense around quarterback Caleb Williams, and Swift has become an important part of that plan.The Bears also have Kyle Monangai in the backfield, giving them a different type of running threat. That combination worked well last season as Chicago produced one of the NFL’s better rushing attacks. Swift’s ability to contribute as both a runner and receiver gives Johnson another reliable option within his offense.There is still a financial calculation behind the decision. Swift will be under contract through age 30, and running back performance can become harder to predict as players get older. Yet Chicago clearly decided his recent production and fit within Johnson’s offense justified the investment.For the Bears, the timing may be the most revealing part. They did not wait for Swift to prove himself all over again in 2026. They saw enough already and chose to secure him before the season began.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Open news: Robert Griffin III toasts 'my guy' Ben Shelton for huge win over Frances Tiafoe
articles.summary: Robert Griffin III wasted no time celebrating Ben Shelton’s breakthrough on Friday night. The former NFL quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner took to social...
articles.body:
Robert Griffin III wasted no time celebrating Ben Shelton's breakthrough on Friday night. The former NFL quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner took to social media shortly after Shelton advanced to his first Grand Slam final , framing the achievement around the history that came with it.

"Congrats to my guy Ben Shelton," Griffin wrote on X, formerly Twitter . "Ben Shelton is the 1st Black American man since Arthur Ashe in 1972 to reach a US Open singles final. Ben Shelton is the 1st Black American man since MaliVai Washington at Wimbledon in 1996 to reach a Grand Slam singles final. His time is now."

Both milestones check out. Ashe won the inaugural US Open in 1968 and returned to the final in 1972, and no Black American man had reached that stage in Flushing Meadows in the 54 years since. Washington's run to the 1996 Wimbledon final, where he lost to Richard Krajicek, stood as the last time a Black American man reached any Grand Slam final until Friday night.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Shelton got there by outlasting good friend and fellow American Frances Tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 at Arthur Ashe Stadium. After a rough opening set that included 14 unforced errors, the No. 8 seed found his rhythm on serve, finishing with 20 aces and 47 winners. The decisive stretch came in a grueling 19-point game to break Tiafoe and close out the third set, and Tiafoe could not recover from there.

The run has been building all week. Shelton knocked off defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a quarterfinal that ended at 3:33 a.m., the latest finish in tournament history, and he is already guaranteed to climb to No. 4 in the world after entering the tournament ranked ninth. He dedicated Friday's win to his grandmother, who died earlier this year and who he credited with introducing his father and coach Bryan to tennis.

Now Shelton faces top seed Alexander Zverev with a chance to end a 23-year drought for American men at the majors, dating back to Andy Roddick's 2003 US Open title. Zverev holds a perfect 5-0 record against him and has won the past 10 sets between them, though the two have never met at a Grand Slam. Griffin, for his part, seems convinced the moment has arrived.

articles.title: What would a successful Week 1 be for the Washington Commanders?
articles.summary: Obviously, the Commanders want to win, but Dan Quinn expresses what he's looking for in Week 1 vs. Eagles.
articles.body:
What does an NFL head coach look for in the first game?

Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn was asked Friday what he was looking for in Sunday's season opener in Philadelphia . Of course, Quinn would like to win the road game against the Eagles , but what would he view as a successful game against the two-time defending NFC East champs?

It's no secret that the Eagles dominated Washington in both games played in Philadelphia during the 2024 season, the second game there being the NFC Championship Game, when the Eagles rolled the Commanders 55-23. Last season, the Eagles won the first meeting 28-19, before resting most starters in the season finale for their playoff game. Washington won that game 24-17.

"Week 1, you want to play with good style," expressed Quinn. "I think that's important. You want to make sure that you're playing with good discipline. That comes in the form of the turnover margin; that comes in the form of penalties, where you're playing as clean as you can."

Last season, the Commanders were penalized one more time than their opponents, 117-116. The Commanders also produced the second-fewest interceptions in 2025, with only eight.

"Those are the things I think in early season that can be the margin. Both sides will have new wrinkles and new looks. That's part of it. Both sides have some new play callers. So, there'll be new looks that they haven't practiced here. So, having the discipline within the system to play it out and fight through the adversity when those come up. We know those happen. So, I think those are some of the key points."

Washington's new coordinators are David Blough (offense) and Daronte Jones (defense), while the Eagles have new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and have retained veteran defensive coordinator Vic Fangio.

articles.title: Lanier rushing attack overpowers Jefferson in district opener
articles.summary: Lanier senior running back Nicholas Torres rushedfor 131 yards and a touchdown in the first half as the Voks defeated Jefferson 31-14 on Friday.
articles.body:
Lanier senior running back Nicholas Torres rushedfor 131 yards and a touchdown in the first half as the Voks defeated Jefferson 31-14 on Friday at the San Antonio ISD Athletic Complex in the two teams' District 14-5A-II opener.

"What I saw on the field was what we went over at practice," Torres said. "We just kept trying to pound the rock and run up the score."

Torres' efforts and a 1-yard rushing touchdown early in the second half from sophomore QB Erick Esparza propelled the Voks to a 17-6 advantage with just under two minutes to play in the third quarter.

After an early score, not much was going for Jefferson on offense, but the Mustangs kept plugging away on the ground, eventually punching in a 6-yard rushing touchdown from senior running back Michael Bejar.

The Mustangs lined up to attempt a 2-point conversion that would cut the deficit down to three, but Mother Nature had other plans as players and coaches were forced off the field due to a lightning delay.

Jefferson waited over two hours for the 2-point play, but the wait was well worth it as Bejar barreled up the A-gap for the conversion.

On the ensuing possession, the Voks got right back to work on the ground, alternating carries between Torres and Esparza. Lanier ran the ball eight consecutive times before Torres found the end zone for his second and final score of the night.

"He had been frustrated with the prior games because he didn't get many touches, but it was strategic," Lanier coach Sal Tellez said of Torres. "We know what we have with him. We have younger backs that we want to get into the rotation and see what they have. When you get in close games, especially in that first half, we wanted to make sure we ran with Nicholas (Torres)."

A quick three-and-out from the Mustangs gave possession back to the Voks. Three plays later, Esparza broke free for a 43-yard rushing touchdown - his second of the night.

"He's a leader," Tellez said of Esparza. "He's a sophomore leader. We have two other quarterbacks. We want to see what we have. So we rode with the other guys in the first half, and then in the second half, we threw Erick in there. And you saw how electrifying he was."

During the lightning delay, Tellez had to keep his players energized.

"When we were in there, we were just talking to them about how important it is to stay focused," Tellez explained. "We gave them bananas. We gave them some oranges. I had some of the parents go buy me some stuff because it was almost 11 p.m. So we knew they were going to be hungry. We knew they wanted to have something in their stomach, and we wanted to make sure we did that. I think that was the key. I think you saw the difference in the second half."

articles.title: “She’s single-handedly catapulted my career.”: How Brittany Mahomes’ unexpected jacket connection helped Kristin Juszczyk turn a memorable Chiefs moment into an NFL licensing deal
articles.summary: NFL News: Kristin Juszczyk had spent years making custom sportswear before one message from Brittany Mahomes helped set up a moment she never expected. The desi.
articles.body: Kristin Juszczyk had spent years making custom sportswear before one message from Brittany Mahomes helped set up a moment she never expected. The designer had already made pieces for NFL stars and other athletes, but her Chiefs jacket reached a much bigger audience on Jan. 13, 2024. That night, Taylor Swift and Brittany wore Kristin’s custom designs during Kansas City’s playoff game against the Miami Dolphins.The connection started with Brittany, but the impact went much further. Swift wearing Kristin’s jacket created huge attention around her work, while the NFL soon gave the designer another major opportunity. Within weeks, Kristin had secured a licensing deal that allowed her to use official NFL logos on her designs.How Brittany Mahomes helped get Kristin Juszczyk’s jacket to Taylor SwiftKristin had already built a name for herself through handmade game-day clothing. Before the Chiefs-Dolphins playoff game, she made a custom Chiefs design for Brittany Mahomes and asked if Brittany could pass another jacket to Taylor Swift.Brittany agreed. Then came the message that Kristin did not expect.During a Feb. 8, 2024, interview, Kristin explained that Brittany contacted her the day before she planned to send the jacket. Brittany asked for a video of Taylor’s jacket, which immediately made Kristin wonder if Swift and Brittany might wear them together.“Brittany texted me and she said, 'Hey, can you send me a video of Taylor’s jacket?' And I was like, 'Wait, is there a possibility the guys both wearing this?' And she said, 'Yeah, we’re wearing it,'" Kristin Juszczyk recalled. "It was just such a pinch me moment. I mean, it just was incredible.”The answer became reality on Jan. 13. Swift and Brittany arrived at the Chiefs’ playoff game in matching red puffer jackets. Swift’s jacket carried Travis Kelce’s name and No. 87, while Brittany’s featured Patrick Mahomes’ No. 15.The images quickly spread across social media. Kristin’s husband, San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk, also stepped in to make sure people knew who designed the jackets. He replied to several posts on X and identified Kristin as the creator.That exposure gave Kristin a career boost she could immediately feel.“She’s single-handedly catapulted my career,” Kristin said about Swift during the Feb. 8 interview. “I’ve been at this for years. When I saw her walk out in that jacket, it just like, brought me to tears.”Kristin said there is another person who she feels she had a hand in her success."I lost my mom when I was 18," she said. "But so much of this just feels like divine. My mom, I just feel like has just made this fate for me." Why the viral Chiefs jacket helped lead Kristin to an NFL licensing dealThe Swift moment did not come out of nowhere. Kristin had spent years creating custom pieces, including designs worn by Simone Biles, Olivia Culpo and Taylor Lautner. Still, the Chiefs jackets put her work in front of an audience far beyond the NFL fashion circle.By Feb. 2024, Kristin had reached a licensing agreement with the NFL that allowed her to use official league logos on her designs. The deal gave her a chance to turn the attention around her custom jackets into officially licensed NFL fashion.Kristin also used the sudden spotlight to give back. In Feb. 2024, she created NFL team-neutral Super Bowl puffer vests for auction and said she planned to donate the proceeds to the National Breast Cancer Foundation.So, while Taylor Swift became the face of the viral fashion moment, Brittany Mahomes played an important role in getting the jacket to her in the first place. One message from Brittany helped bring Kristin’s work to Swift, and that January night helped turn years of sewing and designing into a much bigger NFL business opportunity.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
While Week 1 of the 2026 regular season got underway on Wednesday, the bulk of the schedule remains ahead. Fantasy football managers still have time to adjust lineups, react to Friday's injury reports, and look for replacements on the waiver wire.

Of course, many of the top wire targets were claimed when waivers were processed earlier in the week.

Fortunately, some capable replacements should still be available for the Week 1 slate. Here, you'll find a look at the top remaining plays, the latest buzz and reporting from the NFL's injury report , and a few sleepers to consider ahead of Sunday.

All rankings, picks, and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Quarterbacks around the league are mostly healthy heading into Week 1, though the Atlanta Falcons have some legitimate concerns. Tua Tagovailoa suffered an oblique injury during the week, and both he and Michael Penix Jr. have been ruled out.

This means the Falcons will start backup Cooper Rush against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In larger leagues, Rush could serve as an emergency starter, since he'll at least get to throw to Bijan Robinson, Kyle Pitts, and Drake London. Of course, a road matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers isn't the most enticing option.

New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough is a much more attractive waiver target. He is a viable dual-threat signal-caller, and he'll face a Detroit Lions defense that surrendered the 10th-most fantasy points in 2025.

Malik Willis of the Miami Dolphins and the Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones are two other QBs to consider adding this week.

Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty and Arizona Cardinals rookie back Jeremiyah Love are both dealing with ankle sprains and will bear watching until kickoff.

The good news is that both players appear to be on the mend. Jeanty was a full participant in practice this week and should get the start. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Friday that Love is " trending well ," but will be a game-time decision.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers back Sean Tucker is listed as doubtful, while Saints RB Alvin Kamara is questionable. Dallas Cowboys running back Malik Davis has been ruled out with a hip injury.

Raiders rookie Mike Washington Jr. remains the top RB sleeper, even with Jeanty trending to play. The speedy Arkansas product should get multiple opportunities as a complementary back and will face a Dolphins defense short on star power.

Washington is rostered in just 23.8 percent of leagues. Cardinals back Tyler Allgeier and Jacksonville Jaguars back Chris Rodriguez Jr. are also worth consideration this week. Allgeier is actually listed as RB1 on Arizona's depth chart .

New England Patriots receiver A.J. Brown came out of Wednesday's game with an ankle injury and is headed to injured reserve. San Francisco 49ers rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suffered his own ankle injury on Thursday night and is likely to miss some time.

Fortunately, there isn't an extensive list of injured receivers for the rest of the Week 1 slate. New York Giants receiver Malik Nabers, who is working his way back from a torn ACL, is officially questionable. Buccaneers wideout Jalen McMillan is doubtful with a knee injury. Chicago Bears receiver Rome Odunze (calf) is questionable.

Colts receiver Alec Pierce has been recovering from ankle surgery and dealing with a heel injury but has been cleared for Week 1. Even so, fellow Indy receiver and free-agent addition Keenan Allen is worth considering.

Allen has regularly carried a high PPR floor and will face a Baltimore Ravens defense that surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing WRs last season—though the unit is expected to improve under new head coach Jesse Minter. Allen is rostered in only 15 percent of fantasy leagues.

Ravens rookie Ja'Kobi Lane , Cleveland Browns rookie Denzel Boston , and Raiders receiver Tre Tucker are other receiver targets to consider plucking from the wire this week.

The big injury news at tight end involves Raiders star Brock Bowers. He recently underwent a knee procedure and is expected to miss "a game or two," according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport .

Saints tight end Oscar Delp is out with a hamstring injury.

Fellow Saints tight end Juwan Johnson is a prime waiver target for Week 1. He's likely to be Shough's No. 2 target behind Chris Olave, and he'll be up against a Lions defense with several question marks in the secondary. He should have top-10 value this week but is rostered in just 33.3 percent of fantasy leagues.

Houston Texans tight end Dalton Schultz and Jacksonville Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange are other wire targets who carry top-10 upside.

articles.title: C.J. Stroud is the key to the Texans. But it starts with a new line. Three things to watch vs. Bills
articles.summary: C.J. Stroud's contract future, a rebuilt offensive line and a rematch with Josh Allen are three things to watch when the Texans open their season.
articles.body:
It's two days before the game as we're writing this, and C.J. Stroud 's agent hasn't reached an agreement with the Houston Texans on a contract extension.

There was optimism that a deal could get done before training camp started.

But both sides appear content to push negotiations into the offseason and wait to see how this season plays out first.

That means Stroud will be betting on himself this year, making the 2026 season an all-important one for the fourth-year quarterback.

Stroud played at an elite level as a rookie. But since then, he has finished mostly in the middle of the pack statistically among quarterbacks.

Last season, Stroud played in a new system under new offensive coordinator Nick Caley, and it took him some time to adjust.

But during training camp, he looked much improved from the previous year, taking better command of the offense.

"He's just more dialed into the preparation, more comfortable with the offense," coach DeMeco Ryans told the Houston Chronicle. "It was a quicker training camp with the install. Things were sped up because it's the second time around. So I think that allows him to be more locked in.

"He had an injury last offseason where he couldn't participate. So now he's been healthy all offseason, he's taking care of his body, he looks good, in shape, so I can only imagine what's next for him. …

He has improved his leadership and taken accountability for last season's playoff loss, in which he threw four interceptions, all in the first half.

His play and improvement will be key to Houston's success this season. They also will ultimately determine his future.

A new deal will likely happen next offseason, as there's little reason to believe he will regress.

But a bad season from Stroud might have Houston thinking twice about whether he will be part of its future plans.

The Texans didn't go shopping at Neiman Marcus for offensive linemen in free agency this offseason.

But they did try to add competition on the offensive line, most notably with rookie guard Keylan Rutledge, whom general manager Nick Caserio says might be the best lineman on the team.

That's high praise from Caserio, who doesn't typically crown players before they play in a game.

But the Texans are excited about their first-round rookie. He's relentless, plays to the end of the whistle and sometimes past it. He's not afraid to tussle with other players. And he played well in the preseason.

"I show up every day, work hard," Rutledge said. "There's a certain kind of attitude I bring. There's a certain way I play. Toeing that line, trying to go dominate every play."

He'll make his debut at left guard in the season opener, barring any unexpected injuries.

Rutledge has helped change the mindset of Houston's offensive line, a shift in personality that began last year after Cole Popovich was elevated to offensive line coach. There was a mass exodus of offensive linemen, including Laremy Tunsil , Kenyon Green , Shaq Mason , Juice Scruggs and Tytus Howard .

But the Texans now believe they have the right pieces to achieve the success they're seeking. It took several attempts, but Houston finally found its best starting five before the Raiders preseason game.

The starting unit will consist of second-year lineman Aireontae Ersery , Rutledge, free-agent acquisition Evan Brown , Ed Ingram and Trent Brown .

While Stroud's improvement will be the biggest key for the Texans' offense this season, it will start with the improvement of the offensive line. Protecting Stroud will be paramount.

The Texans were 5-0 when Stroud was sacked once or less and 8-2 when he was sacked twice or less.

"To put that s- on tape," Brown said when asked about the offensive line's goal. "We don't want to dip our toe in the water. We're trying to go out there, first play, game one, and set the tone for who we are."

Brown said he has seen a ton of improvement from last year. Everyone has been on the same page, he said.

"I feel like we can be an elite group," Brown said. "And that's just the goal we're chasing.

"Doing our job and keeping Seven (Stroud) upright so he can do what he does. Because he's special when he has the time."

Can the Texans replicate their success against Josh Allen ?

The last time the Texans faced the Buffalo Bills and quarterback Josh Allen, they sacked him eight times and intercepted him twice. They chased and defended him with a tornado-like intensity.

Ryans likes to call it S.W.A.R.M., which stands for Special Work Ethic and A Relentless Mindset.

It was one of Allen's worst games of the 2025 season.

Meanwhile, the prime-time showing served as an introduction to the Texans' top defense.

But if you talk to players and coaches inside Reliant Stadium, you'd think that performance last year had no bearing on what will happen in their season opener Sunday.

"With this being our first game, anything goes," Ryans said. "Any looks, any type of schemes, anything can come up. For that reason, I don't put a lot of weight into the games that we played prior."

Not to mention, the Bills have a new coaching staff and defensive system.

After longtime Bills coach Sean McDermott was fired last offseason, the Bills elevated offensive coordinator Joe Brady to the role.

Brady then hired Jim Leonhard , who previously was the assistant head coach and pass-game coordinator for the Denver Broncos under Sean Payton and Vance Joseph, as his defensive coordinator.

As for Allen specifically, the Texans know they can't rest on their 2025 performance. As confident as they are in their ability, they know the former MVP - who was voted the second-best player in the NFL this past year by his peers - is too good to assume he'll struggle again.

"He's a great player, dangerous throughout the play," defensive coordinator Matt Burke said. "He has a history of making off-schedule plays and extending plays and creating explosives off that, which is obviously a thing we've talked about a lot."

Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair said the same.

"He's a really great talent, one of the top quarterbacks in the league," he said. "Played at an extremely high level.

"He can pretty much do it all. Run the ball, throw the ball."

Allen, though, hasn't had a great history inside Reliant Stadium. He's 0-4 all time against the Texans in Houston, losing in 2025, 2024, the 2020 playoffs and 2018.

The Texans and their vaunted defense are hoping to make that 0-5.

"It's a whole new season," Al-Shaair said. "We have to put it on tape. Obviously, we think highly of ourselves, but it doesn't mean anything if you don't go do it."

articles.title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 2 of 2026 NCAA Football season
articles.summary: Here are three players Broncos Country should watch in Week 2 of the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the NCAA Football season in the books. Last week, we took a look at a trio of potential first-round prospects that could be of interest to the Denver Broncos in the 2027 NFL Draft. This week we will cover three more players, with varying degrees of potential round placement, for the Week 2 slate of games.

Will Echoles — Defensive Tackle — Ole Miss

The defensive line is a key of the Denver Broncos . It's a position they have acquired quality free agents such as Zach Allen , Malcolm Roach , D.J. Jones . Additionally, the have utilized some early round draft picks (Sai'vion Jones, Tyler Onyedim) the couple of years to address long-term.

It's certainly not a primary need for the Broncos. However, Eyioma Uwazurike is in a contract season and D.J. Jones will be 32 next year and carries over a $14.5 million cap hit. With that in mind, taking a look at this year's class of defensive tackles is worth considering.

Fortifying the defensive line is always a smart move, which makes it potentially in play if the right player is on the clock when the Broncos are picking next April. One player I'm bullish on is Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles.

After a quiet freshman campaign, the former four-star recruit was a fifteen-game starter for the Rebels last season and notched 68 tackles, 11.5 tackles for loss, and 5 sacks. For his efforts, he earned AP first-team All-SEC honors and topped all P4 conference players with 39 quarterback pressures and 35 defensive stops.

He just turned 20 years old and there is no doubt his best football is ahead of him. He is a force against the run and shows great upside as an interior pass rusher. While had a bit of a rough outing in the Rebels' close Week 1 victory over Louisville, Echoles should have a chance to dominate against Charlotte tonight. If he can put it all together this season, I would not be surprised if he wound up being a Top 15 pick next April.

The Broncos enter their 2026 season with Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga slated as their starting duo. It's an underrated group, and they also brought back Taylor Rapp who will eventually see time as a depth player for them this season. Though it's important to note Jones will be a free agent at the end of the season, with Hufanga following suit in 2027.

As far as the rest of the players at the position, their roster is rounded out by Tycen Anderson , Devon Key , and J.L. Skinner. That trio has largely been career contributors on special teams—with their potential as foundational starters in the future unlikely. The team also has '26 NFL Draft selection Miles Scott on their practice squad.

I'll admit that safety isn't a premium position to address in the draft. History shows you can find quality starters at the position on Day 2, even as well as Day 3. One layer I think who will wind up hearing his name called a lot earlier than you think is Oklahoma Sooners standout Peyton Bowen.

After spending his first two years in Norman as mostly a backup contributor and special teams' player, Bowen became a full-time starter in '25 and was a second-team All-SEC selection. He posted 47 tackles, 7 pass breakups, and 2 interceptions. His size (5'11 and 200 pounds) doesn't stand out, but his football play on the field does.

Bowen's football intelligence and positional versatility are huge positives. I feel he has true potential as a single-high player but is also someone who has the chops to man down the nickel position in the NFL. That duality will be highly coveted by scouts and general managers in the coming months looking to bolster their franchise's secondary.

He's just consistent with most everything he does, which is a reason I'll be keeping a close eye on him as the collegiate season continues. You can catch Bowen in action against the Michigan Wolverines in today's early slate of games.

Vicari Swain — Cornerback — South Carolina

Fans might not want me to talk about the potential of Denver opting to use an early round selection on a cornerback in the 2027 NFL Draft, but here we are. I do expect one of Ja'Quan McMillian or Riley Moss to get an extension with the team. However, it seems unlikely both will earn well-deserved extensions.

The good thing is they have 2025 first-round pick Jahdae Barron already as an in-house replacement option for one of them. He has been cross trained at both the slot and boundary spots. While some were down on his lack of impact as a rookie, I'm optimistic about his NFL potential.

The Broncos are facing a situation where their All-Pro return specialist Marvin Mims Jr. may depart in free agency after this season. Finding players with his dynamic return ability are rare. That's why I thought I'd bring up South Carolina cornerback Vicari Swain—who is an impressive cover corner who makes big plays on defense but is also one of the nation's elite punt return specialists.

During his first two seasons with the Gamecocks, Swain (6'0", 193 pounds) was primarily a backup player. Last season, he appeared in every game and had three starts. Even though he wasn't a full-time starter, his impact (especially at slot) was evident with 28 tackles, 1 sack, 2 forced fumbles, along with 2 interceptions and 5 pass breakups. He also had 19 punt returns for 302 yards and three touchdowns.

This season he is poised to make a greater impact for his team. As of now, most outlets have Swain as Day 2 selection. While he doesn't have a tough matchup this week, you can catch him this evening when South Carolina hosts Towson.

articles.title: Stan Verrett on the ‘fantastic’ feeling of being back at ESPN
articles.summary: Some might have been surprised to see Stan Verrett back in ESPN’s orbit, but not him. Verrett, who left the Worldwide Leader last year, has returned as host...
articles.body:
Some might have been surprised to see Stan Verrett back in ESPN's orbit , but not him.

Verrett, who left the Worldwide Leader last year, has returned as host of NFL Total Access on NFL Network. NFL Total Access originally ended in May 2024 , but after ESPN acquired NFL Network, the powers that be decided to revive the show.

The new NFL Total Access debuted on Sept. 8 and will air Tuesday through Friday from noon to 2 p.m. ET. Verrett has stayed busy over the past year. The New Orleans native hosted a digital pregame show for the Saints and appeared on the L.A. Clippers, NBA TV, and FanDuel Sports Network, as well as a Twitch show with his former SportsCenter co-anchor, Neil Everett.

We recently caught up with Verrett to discuss his new job.

Note: This interview has been edited and condensed for length and clarity.

Stan Verrett: "It's fantastic. One of my goals when I got to ESPN in 2000 was to do SportsCenter for a while and then eventually cover the NFL because it's always been my passion since I was a little kid. I was never more excited than when the Saints had a home game in New Orleans. I could barely sleep on Saturday nights because I've had season tickets since I was 12. That's what made me choose this profession: a chance to express my love of football and have a job that doesn't really feel like a job. During football season, I spend a lot of time watching and talking about football with other people. This gives me a chance to really focus on it and serve the fans."

"Mike McQuade, an executive at ESPN, was the guy who hired me back in 2000. He mentioned that when I left, ESPN was purchasing the NFL Network and that there might be a chance for me to come back to work in L.A. So you never count those things until the name is on the contract. And so I just set about doing other stuff. And then it became real. Here I am back again, and I feel I have a whole lot of new skills in my toolbox to bring to this job.

"I would have stayed at SportsCenter forever here in L.A. I would have stayed at that job as long as they would have me, but it got disrupted. Now I look back on the past year, and it was really, really good for my skills as a sports broadcaster because I did a lot of different things I hadn't done before."

How does this version of NFL Total Access differ from the previous one?

"I wouldn't really compare it. I think the most important thing for me is to give people who tune in the most information they can get from anywhere about what's going on in the NFL. Compiling that information, learning it, and getting it comes naturally to me because I've been doing it since I can remember football. I could never know enough about the NFL based on my fandom for the Saints. I wanted to know everything about what was going on with the Saints. And then, expanding on that, I wanted to know everything that was going on around the rest of the league. It's just always been a thing."

How would you persuade someone to watch this show?

"If you want to know what's going on in the NFL from a holistic perspective, across every team, it's the place to tune in because the show has unlimited access to the NFL. The cameras are right there at every facility. So, we just fire up the cameras when somebody shows up, and then we add perspective and analysis to what they say. You get an unfiltered look at what coaches and players have to say, and then you get perspective and analysis, hopefully from what we add to their comments."

And you're going to work from Los Angeles?

"Absolutely. It's a fantastic situation. As I said, it's really interesting how things worked out. I'm still going to be at NBA TV. I really enjoy it, and I want to make sure I can continue doing it. The great thing about Total Access , too, is that it's from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m. Pacific time. So around 11:30, I'm out the door. In the afternoons and evenings, I can do other things. NBA TV has been great, and I want to continue doing it. So I'm going to be doing a bunch of Saturdays with NBA TV because they're adding live programming on Saturdays now."

Will you still be doing the Saints pregame show?

"We're not doing this show live from the Superdome anymore. We found out that competing with the broadcast pregame shows was tough, especially because our most loyal audience, Saints fans, were on their way to the game. So they weren't able to tune in to the show the way we were doing it. We were doing it like it was a television show. So now we're doing a preview podcast. It's called The Snap with Stan Verrett , and it's going to be on NewOrleansSaints.com starting on Friday throughout the weekend so people can tune in whenever they want."

What do you think is the biggest question mark for the Saints this season?

"How quickly they can grow up together. They've gone from a veteran team to a very young team very quickly. So there are a lot of young guys they're going to be counting on to deliver this season. Jonas Sanker on defense. Tyler Shough on offense. Barion Brown , a rookie who looks like he's going to play a pivotal role this season. Two young offensive tackles who were first-round picks. A lot of young guys are going to need to be productive and play. So I think that's the biggest X factor. How well can these young guys come together, individually and collectively, and deliver for the team?"

Are you still doing The Stan and Neil Show on Twitch with Neil Everett?

"We're working that out to figure out where we're going to do the podcast this season. Our plan is to continue, but we're going to make some changes, and we haven't really ironed that out yet."

Has this been a time crunch for you, handling all these different jobs?

"It only became a scheduling issue once last season, when the Clippers had a Saturday game, and I had the Sunday show in New Orleans, live at the Superdome the next morning. I did the Clippers game, took a red-eye, and would have made it. Everything would have gone fine, but there were weather problems in New Orleans. It was really foggy, and for a couple of hours, no planes could land. I got stuck in Houston, waiting for the all-clear to get to New Orleans.

"Scott Shanle, our analyst on the show, is in Dallas, and it's an hour-long flight. He would fly in on Sunday mornings, too. He couldn't get there either. We weren't able to do the show. But barring the weather, I would have made it."

If you need to impress an out-of-towner, which New Orleans restaurant do you take them to?

"If somebody's on an expense account and doesn't have to pay for the meal, and they want a world-class New Orleans meal, it's hard to beat Commander's Palace . It's fantastic. But if you want a down-home feel for the city and the cuisine that makes New Orleans so special, Li'l Dizzy's in Treme. It's the Baquet family, a black family that has owned restaurants in New Orleans for decades. It's got fried chicken and gumbo, along with other New Orleans specialties they do really well. Every day there's a line down the street to get in. It's hard to walk up and get a table there because the food is so good."

articles.title: In Year 11, a look at how the Cardinals' Jacoby Brissett views his world
articles.summary: Jacoby Brissett has never produced a winning record as an NFL starting quarterback, but he fits well with Mike LaFleur's offense in Arizona.
articles.body:
In his 10 NFL seasons, Jacoby Brissett has started three season openers. On two other occasions, he was inserted as the starter by Week 2. So, in some sense, he'll be no stranger to the stage on Sunday, Sept. 13, when he takes the first snap of a new Arizona Cardinals season.

Thing is, none of those previous occasions have been remotely normal.

With the 2016 Patriots, Brissett started in Week 2 after Tom Brady was suspended due to "Deflategate."

A year later, he was traded to the Colts in early September after a season-ending injury to Andrew Luck , and started just 15 days later. In 2019, he started a career-high 15 games thanks to Luck's shocking preseason retirement. Then came the 2022 Browns, when Brissett became the Week 1 starter only after Deshaun Watson 's August suspension for sexual misconduct.

Two years later, Brissett was back in New England , starting temporarily before rookie Drake Maye earned his job.

That is quite the list. Using only those seasons, you could tell a fairly complete history of the NFL's past decade's worth of off-field turmoil. For most players, it's a cliché, but Brissett has truly seen it all.

This summer, then, has offered a reprieve. A minor contract squabble, solved before the end of July? That's small potatoes in his world.

"I definitely feel a lot more comfortable now than I did the other times that I was the Week 1 starter," Brissett said.

Brissett has spent the past six weeks studying LaFleur's offense and practicing in it every day. And he has a year's worth of rapport with Trey McBride , Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson — all of whom he regularly stays with after practice, getting in extra reps.

That should bring tangible benefits on Sundays. Brissett can play faster now, with less thinking. Envision a back-shoulder pass placed exactly where the receiver needs it, or a layered pass over the middle, because he knows how each concept is designed to attack each coverage.

Plus, this is an offense that — in theory — meshes with Brissett's skill set.

When asked about that fit, LaFleur and Brissett were both coy, with the quarterback jokingly asking a reporter, "You work for the Chargers?"

"When we're under center in play action, lot of times, the quarterback has to turn his back to the defense," Harrison said. "Some quarterbacks don't like to do that. I think that's one of (Brissett's) strong suits, him being able to do that."

When lined up under center last season, Brissett averaged 7.4 yards per attempt, the league average among qualified quarterbacks. From the shotgun, that dropped to 6.8 yards per attempt, ranking 21st among 32 quarterbacks.

And across the NFL, no team attempted more passes from under center in 2025 than the Los Angeles Rams , where LaFleur was the offensive coordinator.

"If you're just in the gun, you keep your eyes on the defense the whole time, you get to see the rotations," Harrison said. "But if the quarterback turns his back to the defense, you don't know where the safeties are gonna be. Everybody in the league does a good job disguising at this point."

Diagnosing those disguises without being able to watch them in action requires a certain mental acuity. And that, Harrison believes, is one of Brissett's greatest strengths.

"Being able to turn your back to the defense and still process things at a quick pace, I think that's very important under Coach LaFleur," Harrison said.

In the big picture, it's hard to know how much any of this will matter for the Cardinals. Making a playoff push this season would require a miracle, and the organization will likely look to acquire its quarterback of the future this offseason.

But Brissett can help establish stability under a new regime, creating foundations that last until long after he's gone.

And, on a personal level, there's a player entering his 11th season with his sixth team, still trying to prove that he can lead a winning team. The NFL doesn't allow much space for emotion or reflection, but as a new season arrives, Brissett took a moment for both.

"If the ultimate thing doesn't happen for me, I can honestly say I've accomplished a lot of goals that I didn't think were even possible to set for myself that I'm still chasing," Brissett said. "When I look back, I'm going into Year 11, I didn't think I was making it past two, to be honest with you.

articles.title: 2027 NFL Mock Draft: Darian Mensah, Trinidad Chambliss Join Dante Moore, Arch Manning in Round 1
articles.summary: The college football season is entering Week 2 and the NFL season is just getting started, which means 2027 NFL mock drafts are also in full effect. Early in...
articles.body:
The college football season is entering Week 2 and the NFL season is just getting started, which means 2027 NFL mock drafts are also in full effect.

Early in the college football season, several players have put their names on the NFL Draft radar, and they have the rest of 2026 to prove why they should be selected on Day 1.

Now, in Week 1 of the NFL season, let's use PFN's Mock Draft Simulator to project how the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft currently stacks up.

In my last mock draft , we had some fun as the New York Jets acquired the No. 1 overall pick in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. However, in this go-around, we'll get straight to business, leading the Cardinals to draft a new franchise quarterback in Dante Moore.

Arizona recently extended Michael Wilson , and Marvin Harrison Jr. will be looking for an extension of his own next offseason. It's crucial for Arizona to find its gunslinger of the future.

As for Moore, he is the No. 1-ranked quarterback on PFN's 2027 NFL Draft Big Board . With this season of development, there is a legitimate chance the Oregon product will be ready to start on Sundays as a rookie.

A no-brainer decision for the Miami Dolphins, bringing home Jeremiah Smith not only gives them the best receiver in the draft but also gives the fans a reason to show up and show out in the midst of a rebuild.

Considered a perennial top-five selection since his first snap at Ohio State, Smith already began the year with an electric performance, as he put up 151 yards and 2 touchdowns in the first half against Ball State. Smith is picking up right where he left off and proving to scouts that he's still the best receiver in college football.

As of now, Arch Manning is still the only other quarterback who could claim the QB1 slot in the 2027 NFL Draft. Still, with Dante Moore going No. 1 overall, this gives the New York Jets a chance to build around the 6-foot-4, mobile Manning, with several talented pieces already around their quarterback of the future.

It's clear that Geno Smith is nothing more than a bridge quarterback for the 2026 season, so the Jets will likely be all-in on finding a face of the franchise after this year. Manning is expected to lead Texas through a competitive SEC, so perhaps a CFP run and Heisman trophy push would make him a lock to be one of the top two quarterbacks in 2027.

There just doesn't seem to be a light at either end of the tunnel when it comes to the Cleveland Browns' quarterback options this season. Whether it's Shedeur Sanders , Deshaun Watson , or even Dillon Gabriel , none of these quarterbacks should be starting for Cleveland in 2027.

This takes us to Miami's Darian Mensah, another rising talent in next year's draft class who not only has a strong resume but also the skill set to back it up. He started his 2026 campaign with a 400-yard, 5-touchdown outing, putting him in early Heisman conversations.

A run at the Heisman trophy and a CFP push for the Hurricanes just may be the bump Mensah needs to become a legitimate first-round candidate.

This is almost a no-brainer selection when you look at the Las Vegas Raiders' depth chart, as drafting Texas WR Cam Coleman will instantly provide the offense with a legitimate WR1 candidate and also help relieve some pressure from the team's leading pass catcher, tight end Brock Bowers .

After selecting Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft, giving him a legitimate weapon on the outside has to be priority No. 1 for Las Vegas. Given that the franchise has already heavily invested in the offense over the past few years, a new wide receiver in the first round could be on schedule for the Raiders.

The Atlanta Falcons are a tricky team to project in mock drafts due to the lingering questions surrounding the quarterback position. After investing the No. 8 overall pick in Michael Penix Jr. in 2024, perhaps Atlanta holds off on taking another early-round arm and instead reinforces its offensive line to not only keep Penix upright, but also keep Bijan Robinson happy, too.

Jake Matthews has been a steady presence for over a decade, but he's in the later stages of his career, and the Falcons need a young tackle ready to take the baton. Jordan Seaton was starting in a Power Four conference from the moment he stepped on campus, and he's only gotten more polished since.

Taking Seaton here gives Atlanta a cornerstone blocker who can protect its young passer, open lanes for its star back, and keep the offense on track for the next decade.

The Tennessee Titans spent the last few drafts rebuilding their offense, and now it's time to give the defense a real closer off the edge. With Jermaine Johnson II heading into the final year of his rookie deal, the Titans can't afford to wait on finding their next long-term pass rusher if an extension isn't on the horizon.

Colin Simmons brings the kind of first-step burst that makes tackles panic before the snap, and he's already making his presence felt this fall with a fumble recovery in the opener. He's the type of player who changes games in the fourth quarter, and pairing him with Jeffery Simmons up front would give Tennessee a disruptive duo to build the defense around.

The Carolina Panthers have their lockdown corner on one side with Jaycee Horn , but the spot opposite him is still a question mark. Leonard Moore has been battle-tested since he was a freshman and is now regarded as the best cornerback in the class.

His length and patience in press coverage make him a natural fit for a secondary that wants to play aggressive man coverage, and he allows the Panthers to form a young corner tandem that could hold up against anyone in the division.

The New Orleans Saints' pass rush has leaned on veterans for years, and that window is closing. Quincy Rhodes Jr. out of Arkansas offers a massive frame with long arms that let him win the leverage battle before blockers can get their hands on him.

He's still ascending, which is exactly what a rebuilding defense should want at this spot. New Orleans gets a high-ceiling rusher who can set the edge against the run on Day 1 while his pass-rush game keeps developing.

The New York Giants have always believed games are won in the trenches, and David Stone fits that identity perfectly. He's a former blue-chip recruit with rare power for his size and he's capable of collapsing the pocket from the interior, where quarterbacks feel the most pressure.

Adding him to a defensive front that already has talent on the edges would make it nearly impossible for offenses to slide protection to one side without paying for it elsewhere.

The Washington Commanders need more youth and range on the back end, and Tae Johnson brings a smart, instinctive presence to the secondary.

Notre Dame's defense asks its safeties to handle a lot mentally, and he's comfortable rotating late, disguising coverages, and coming downhill to make tackles in space.

He'd give the Commanders a versatile chess piece who can play deep, drop into the box, or match up with tight ends in an NFC East loaded with weapons.

After moving on from Sauce Gardner , the Jets continue to have a hole at the premium position in their secondary, and Ellis Robinson IV is the perfect candidate to fill it.

Georgia's defense produces pro-ready corners year after year, and he's cut from that same cloth with fluid hips, sticky coverage, and the confidence to challenge receivers at the catch point. New York rebuilds its cornerback room with a player who can grow into a true CB1.

As the backfield ages, the offense needs a young runner to carry the load for the Minnesota Vikings. Miami's Jadan Baugh runs with a downhill style that wears defenses down as the game goes on, but he also has enough burst to turn a simple inside run into a chunk play.

In an offense that thrives on play-action, having a back that defenses actually fear makes everything else easier, especially for a young quarterback still finding his footing.

The Pittsburgh Steelers have been searching for their long-term answer at quarterback since Ben Roethlisberger retired, and Trinidad Chambliss might be the most intriguing option in this class. His journey from Division II to leading an SEC offense shows toughness and a chip on his shoulder that fits the Steelers' culture.

He extends plays with his legs, throws with confidence off-platform, and has a knack for rising in big moments. Pittsburgh finally takes its swing at the position instead of patching it with veterans.

With their second pick in the first round, the Jets give their offense another weapon. Garrett Wilson needs a running mate who can take attention away from him and let rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. thrive as well.

The Jets decide to dip back into the Indiana factory once again, selecting Charlie Becker, who has shown he can stretch the field and win in contested situations. His ability to create explosive plays makes him an ideal complement, giving whoever is under center in New York a much bigger margin for error.

The Chicago Bears' defense still needs another pass rusher to go with Montez Sweat . Dylan Stewart is one of the most explosive edge players in the country, with the twitch and bend to flatten around the corner in a flash.

Stewart plays with a relentless motor that shows up on every down for his team. He did fall in this week's mock draft simply because he missed Week 1 with a back injury, which may also keep him out of Week 2's contest, raising some concern about his medicals.

The Cincinnati Bengals have invested heavily in keeping franchise quarterback Joe Burrow upright, but both starting guards are on a limited time, and the line needs a long-term piece in the middle.

Austin Siereveld fits that need perfectly. He's a physical, heavy-handed blocker with experience lining up at multiple spots, giving the Bengals flexibility if injuries hit.

The Jacksonville Jaguars have talent coming off the edges, but the interior needs someone who can command double teams and free up those rushers. Scott is a thick, powerful tackle who plays with surprising quickness off the snap, and he has a habit of living in the backfield before guards can get set.

Putting him in the middle of the Jaguars' front gives their edge players more one-on-one chances and makes the defense far tougher to run on.

Mississippi State's Kelley Jones brings a long, rangy frame that lets him disrupt receivers at the line, a profile that has become the prototype in today's NFL. Tampa Bay's defense requires corners who can hold up on an island, and Jones can do just that.

He's a natural competitor at the catch point, and he gives the Bucs a young cornerback who can match up with the big-bodied receivers they face in the NFC South.

Denver's defense has become one of the most feared units in the league, thanks in part to its pass rush, and the smart move is keeping that pipeline full. Yhonzae Pierre is a rusher who wins with speed and a nonstop motor, the kind of player who offensive coordinators have to account for on every snap.

Adding him to an already deep rotation would keep the Broncos' pressure relentless for all four quarters and set them up for the future as contracts come due.

The Houston Texans have built a young, confident defense, and KJ Bolden would slide right into that identity. Coming out of Georgia's system, he's used to handling a heavy mental load, and he has the range to cover ground from the deep middle while still showing up as a physical tackler near the line of scrimmage.

He's a former top recruit who plays like it, and he gives the Texans a secondary with the speed and versatility to keep up with any offense in the league.

With Lane Johnson in the later stages of his career, Texas offensive lineman Trevor Goosby is the perfect succession plan. He's a long, athletic tackle with the footwork to mirror speed rushers and the frame to keep adding strength.

The Philadelphia Eagles can develop him behind their veterans and hand him the keys when the time comes, keeping one of the NFL's best lines rolling and one of the top backfields protected.

Detroit's aggressive defensive style puts a lot of pressure on its cornerbacks, and adding another young, competitive corner makes sense, especially given Terrion Arnold 's departure in the offseason.

Ashton Hampton fits the Lions' gritty mentality and gives them a secondary that can hold up against the high-powered passing attacks they'll see deep into January.

Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh wants a defense that plays fast and physical, and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa checks both boxes.

He's an instinctive linebacker who flies sideline to sideline, fills running lanes with bad intentions, and has the athleticism to hang with backs and tight ends in coverage. He'd give Los Angeles a three-down linebacker who can be the heartbeat of the defense for years to come.

Protecting Drake Maye is New England 's top priority, and Carter Smith keeps that mission going. He's a steady, technically sound tackle who helped anchor one of the most impressive offenses in college football.

Smith plays with patience and balance in pass protection and has the toughness to finish blocks in the run game. Pairing him with the Patriots' existing young linemen gives them a foundation up front that could last a long time.

The San Francisco 49ers and Kyle Shanahan's offense depend on its line executing a zone-heavy run scheme with precision, and Minnesota's Greg Johnson has the mobility and awareness to thrive in it.

He gets to the second level quickly, seals off linebackers, and keeps his feet moving through contact. With the 49ers needing to get younger and cheaper on the interior, Johnson is a plug-and-play option who fits the system from Day 1.

If George Pickens walks in free agency, Dallas can't leave CeeDee Lamb without a legit running mate. ASU's Omarion Miller is a dynamic playmaker who can line up outside and take the top off a defense, but he's also dangerous after the catch on quick throws.

The Sun Devil would give the Cowboys a young, explosive target to keep defenses from rolling coverage toward Lamb and ensure the passing game doesn't miss a beat.

Kansas City 's championship formula starts with keeping Patrick Mahomes comfortable, and the tackle spots have been a recurring concern. Melvin Siani is a physical blocker with the size to handle bull rushers and the grit to hold up in big moments.

Adding him gives the Chiefs a young bookend who can grow into a starter and give their star quarterback the time he needs to create magic.

Baltimore always values smart, physical defensive backs, and Miami's OJ Frederique Jr. is just the player this describes. He earned playing time early in his college career and has only gotten better, showing strong instincts, quick recovery speed, and a willingness to come up and tackle.

Giving the Ravens another young corner to go alongside their talented secondary helps them stay ahead in a division full of explosive receivers.

A'Mauri Washington is a massive, powerful interior lineman who eats up blockers and makes it hard for offenses to run between the tackles.

His ability to push the pocket from the inside creates chances for everyone else on the front, and he gives the Seahawks a cornerstone in the middle of their defense for years to come.

DJ Moore was a great addition to provide Josh Allen a legit WR1 on the outside, but other than Khalil Shakir , the Bills really don't have much firepower at the receiver position. Granted, Skyler Bell is still set to kick off his rookie season as the WR3/4 for Buffalo, so that remains to be seen.

Still, the Bills should be all in on finding a young, dynamic weapon for their offense, given that the Keon Coleman experiment has failed. Indiana's Nick Marsh would give the receiving room a significant boost and a legitimate trio of playmakers at wideout.

With Myles Garrett gone, Cleveland has a massive void to fill on the edge, and there's no replacing a player like that with a stopgap. The Browns need a young rusher who can solidify the defensive front alongside Jared Verse and Mason Graham . Oregon's Matayo Uiagalelei has the tools to grow into that role.

Uiagalelei may not be asked to carry the pass rush on Day 1, but he has the size, motor, and upside to become the new tone-setter for a defense searching for its next identity.
